answer: A market's governance kernel grants each public key one vote per round only after a $3 token burn. The ledger binds each burn receipt to that key and round and rejects reuse. Registering agents called umber and shale requires two separate burns, even under one owner. The attacker's marginal cost is an unrecoverable $3 plus transaction fees for every extra voting identity in every round; free key generation no longer creates free influence.
